_note: Scripted replay for development and demos without a Meta API key. Runs that use it are labelled 'replay'. Answers cite evidence IDs and contain no measured numbers.

facts.statement: Each order-list request issues many SQL statements; the count grows with the number of orders and line items on the page.
Most request time is spent waiting on the database.
load_order_details queries order_items once per order and products once per line item.

hypotheses.statement: An N+1 query pattern in load_order_details dominates p95 latency; batching item and product lookups into one query should lower it.
Connection pool waits add latency under load because each request holds many short queries.

missing_information: Query plans for order_items and products lookups
Pool wait time separated from query execution time
content.priority: Remove per-order and per-item queries in load_order_details without changing the response.

content.hypothesis: The N+1 pattern in load_order_details dominates p95; fetching all items of the page with one JOIN removes most queries.
content.expected_effect: SQL statements per request drop to a small constant and p95 falls well past the 20% target at the same arrival rate.
content.falsified_if: p95 improves by less than 20% in the paired runs, or any golden case changes.

patch.summary: Load every line item of the page with one JOIN query instead of one query per order and per item.
